classification.difficultyReason: Requires modelling upstream and downstream speeds using the current, then forming and solving a linear equation.

content.prompt: A river flows at 5 km/h. A boat goes upstream half as fast as downstream. What is the speed of the boat in still water?

answer.short:
$15\text{ km/h}$.

Subtract the current speed upstream and add it downstream; the upstream speed is half the downstream speed.
answer.worked:
Let $v$ be the boat’s speed in still water, in km/h. Its upstream speed is $(v-5)$ km/h and its downstream speed is $(v+5)$ km/h.

$$\begin{align*}v-5&=\frac{v+5}{2}\\2v-10&=v+5\\v-10&=5\\v&=15\end{align*}$$

The boat’s speed in still water is $15\text{ km/h}$. Upstream it travels at $10\text{ km/h}$ and downstream at $20\text{ km/h}$, so the upstream speed is half the downstream speed.
